Note, this is an anime film. A link to the film can be found here. It's 1hr 40min long.

After receiving a recommendation from a friend to check out Ninja Scroll (which I recently reviewed here ), I watched the whole, short filmography of director Yoshiaki Kawajiri. Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust is his final directorial work, and the only one which was released after Ninja Scroll. And it is probably his best work, in my opinion. Also note that this film was originally released in select US theatres and made specifically for an American audience.

The film is based on a Japanese novel series called "Vampire Hunter D", which is based on, well, a vampire hunter named D. It is set in the distant future, and incorporates some sci-fi elements into the gothic vampire genre. The first film adaptation was released in 1985 (which is also on Youtube), but quite frankly, it was not very good. Although Bloodlust is technically a sequel to the 1985 film, you really don't need to watch it. All you need to know is that D is a half-human, half-vampire vampire hunter. It's inferred that he is the son of Dracula, most powerful and noble of the vampires. His left hand is a character in itself, which possesses its own personality and powers.

This movie is pretty good, especially if you are a fan of horror films. There is a certain refinement and classiness about it that I haven't seen in American horror films for a long time. The Japanese handling of the western vampire genre is absolutely excellent. Maybe the closest comparison to this film is Van Helsing.

The animation is some great 2D hand drawn stuff. This time period in some ways was the zenith of the good ole fashioned hand drawn animation. The lines are crisp. There is excellent contrast between light and dark. Overall, this is just a good lookin movie with some exceptionally beautiful scenes.

The direction of the movie is great, almost cinematic at times. The scenes are directed like that of a movie. Fight scenes are pretty good. There is some resemblance to some of Kawajiri's previous works, including Ninja Scroll. The demons all have unique characteristics, and the main hero wields a sword.

One of the highlights in my opinion is the music. The music is just excellent. It elevates the movie to a grand, epic level. The music really shines at the beginning of the movie, but it fits well throughout. Additionally, the voice acting is good. The film was actually originally released in English, so there is no Japanese voice acting.

The story features your standard horror movie fare, but is strong enough that it holds your attention throughout. There is good character development. And what really strengthens it are some of the themes it subtly explores, like what it means to basically be an immortal on earth. There's no sex/nudity and the violence isn't as gruesome as Ninja Scroll, but the film still carries a serious and mature vibe that can definitely be appealing to older and younger viewers alike. The film has both a strong beginning and end, and never really has any down points.

Overall, this film was refreshing. The production quality is high, with the film excelling in multiple regards. Surprisingly, I actually found that this film is better than Ninja Scroll in that it was so refined in mulitple aspects, particularly in the music and story. I am not actually a huge horror fan, so it surprised me just how much I liked this film. They really don't make horror films like this anymore. It is a sophisticated and respectful treatment of the vampire genre, which has been lacking in the US scene for a while. For anyone with an itch for a decent, classy horror film, I would highly recommend Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust. It might possibly be the best vampire film you have ever watched.
